title: Dispatch OGF 9: Rill Orchard Reopens Without Its Glass Harvest
summary: The city preserves the fruit, the warnings, and a question about what the trees saw.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Engineers have rebuilt the Northmere channel and begun a slow refill of the reservoir. Residents of the northern quarter are returning in stages. The council has recorded the evacuation routes used on 22 July alongside the images that first prompted their inspection.

The mirrorwood branches were removed from Rill Orchard yesterday. The remaining trees bear ordinary green fruit. Mrs. Rill has kept one cloudy pear that once showed Peter leaving by the gate. She says she no longer needs it opened: “I know he turned back to look.”

The Institute has catalogued thirty-one glass fruit. Most scenes have faded. Three retain faint images, including the unidentified room reported after the flood. Dr. Saye has sealed them for study, with access limited to the people depicted if they can be identified. The council has agreed that the earlier private scenes will not be displayed.

Inspector Voss’s report credits the advance evacuation with allowing the lower quarter to be cleared before the wall failed. It does not credit the orchard with knowledge of a fixed future. Both the flooded archive step and the dry North Loom Street appeared in fruit from the same branch; the city saw parts of each.

At dusk, our reporter walked with Mrs. Rill between the remaining trees. Their fruit held no rooms or faces. From the ridge, the repaired reservoir was visible above Alderwick. Mrs. Rill said Peter had wanted the orchard to remember one place as it had been. For a few weeks, it seemed to remember several ways the city might become.
